title: Lifting a formally smooth complete local algebra along a finite residually trivial map
statement: Let $\alpha:(A_0,\mathfrak m_0)\to(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings which are complete ($\mathfrak m_0$-adically, resp. $\mathfrak m_A$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]), such that $A$ is a finitely generated $A_0$-module via $\alpha$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $\alpha$ induces an isomorphism of residue fields $A_0/\mathfrak m_0\xrightarrow{\sim}A/\mathfrak m_A=:k$. Let $\varphi:A\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] local homomorphism into a Noetherian local ring which is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete, such that the closed fibre $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$. Then there exist a Noetherian local ring $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ which is $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, a local homomorphism $\gamma:A_0\to C$ such that $C$ is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology, and a local homomorphism $\psi:C\to B$ with $\psi\circ\gamma=\varphi\circ\alpha$, such that the ring map $C\otimes_{A_0}A\to B$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $c\otimes a\mapsto\psi(c)\varphi(a)$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (remark-what-does-it-mean, line 10308), parts (3) and (4), with Lemma Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs, line 10256) and Lemma 07NJ (lift-continuous); as used in the proof of Proposition 07PM (fs-regular, line 12028), second paragraph, where 'completion in the tensor product is not needed as A_0 -> A is finite' by Algebra Lemma 00MA (completion-tensor). Formal smoothness of A_0 -> C in the source is Definition 07NI with A_0 m_0-adic; for a local homomorphism it is the condition of def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic (Lemma 07EC(2))

proof.text: Obtain C, γ, and θ:C→E from [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-closed-fiber-model]. It supplies completeness, Noetherianity, adic formal smoothness, θ surjective, ker θ=m₀C and θγ=πφα.

Put J=m_A B≤m_B. The private proved helper closed_ideal_of_complete_local applies Krull intersection to the Noetherian local quotient B/J and gives J=⋂_{n≥1}(J+m_B^n). Surjectivity of θ makes it local. Convert θ to an A₀-algebra map using its compatibility. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with I=m_B, J, r=t=1. The continuity bound puts ψ(m_C)⊆m_B, hence ψ is local, and algebra compatibility gives ψγ=φα. The lifting equation identifies πψ=θ.

Construct ψ and φ as A₀-algebra maps to B, using the structure via φα. The tensor pushout productMap gives the actual F:D=C⊗_{A₀}A→B, with F(c⊗a)=ψ(c)φ(a). Finite A₀-module generators of A give finite C-module generators of D.

D is m_C-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian]; equivalently it is complete for I=m_C D. F maps I to m_C B, an ideal contained in m_B by locality of ψ. Krull intersection makes B Hausdorff for this ideal. [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coefficient-tensor-reduction-surjective] gives surjectivity of F modulo m_C B. [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] therefore makes F surjective. This replaces the original finite-generators lifting via finite-over-complete-ring.

D is Noetherian because it is finite over C. For any maximal ideal M of D, integrality of C→D gives M∩C=m_C. The balancing equality and locality of γ make (M∩A)∩A₀=m₀. Since A is integral over A₀, the prime M∩A is maximal, hence equals m_A. Thus L=m_A D lies in every maximal ideal M, so L≤jacobson(0). This uses integrality directly rather than the nilpotence-power detour for the Jacobson bound.

From πψ=θ and ker θ=m₀C, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coefficient-tensor-kernel-reduction] gives K≤LK for K=ker F. Noetherianity of D makes K finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] with the just-proved Jacobson containment to get K=0; RingHom.injective_iff_ker_eq_bot makes F injective.
Combine injectivity and surjectivity of the explicitly constructed F, and return C, γ and ψ with the instances and properties already established. The target theorem signature is unchanged.
